earnings.title: Church & Dwight Co., Inc.
highlights: Consumer Domestic net sales were $1,225 million, a $5 million or 0.4% increase.
Consumer International net sales were $297 million, a $7 million or 2.5% increase.
The Specialty Products division also delivered a strong organic sales growth of 5.0% as the business delivered balanced results across the globe.

Global e-commerce revenues grew 20% in the third quarter with global online sales now representing 25.9% of the Company’s total consumer sales, reflecting the continued strength of its digital capabilities and brands.
Organic sales increased 4.4%driven by volume growth (+3.6%) and favorable price and product mix (+0.8%).

quotes.text: Innovation has always been a key driver of our organic growth and it continues to be a major driver of our results in 2026.

outlook: Net sales increased 1.0% to $1,602 million in the third quarter, exceeding the Company’s outlook of a 1% decline and reflecting the benefits of the 2025 strategic portfolio actions.
Organic sales grew 5.1%, well above the Company’s 3% outlook, with growth across all three divisions, driven primarily by volume growth of 4.6%, as well as positive price and mix of 0.5%.
The Company expects full-year capital expenditures to be approximately $125 million or 2% of sales.
“We have revised our reported sales to approximately 0.5%growth, versus our prior view of flat to 1%.

items.heading: A continued change in the retail environment and changing consumer preferences could cause our sales to decline.
Volatility and increases in the price of raw and packaging materials or energy costs could erode our profit margins.
Loss of any of our principal customers could significantly decrease our sales and profitability.
Market category declines and changes to our product and geographic mix may impact the achievement of our sales growth targets, planned pricing and financial results.
We may be unable to successfully identify, finance, complete and integrate future strategic acquisitions, or successfully complete or realize the anticipated benefits of strategic divestitures.
New products and product line extensions may not gain widespread customer acceptance, may be otherwise discontinued, or cause sales of existing products to decline.
